names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 14 aprilie, «Sfânta Muceniță Tomaida».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Απριλίου, «Αγία Θωμαΐς», with the rank word left off; the life page heads her «Αγια Θωμαϊς».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 13 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. муч. Томаида.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with муч. left off as well, the rank word this source uses for a martyr, which this folder already carries in `types`. The heading leaves no epithet and does not name Alexandria, which is the first word of the body; the city is what distinguishes her from `thomais-of-lesbos`, and this corpus keeps such a thing in the display name. No other folder holds a Serbian Томаида.

Read out of the title on the name link behind this place in the line for 13 апреля ст. ст., name page 2739, «Фомаида Александрийская (Египетская), мц.», with the rank word left off. Both epithets are kept because the calendar's own link gives both and the day's line gives only the second: the line declines her as «Фомаиды Египетской», and a bare «Фомаида» would be something reconstructed from the link with less of it in. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form, with or without the brackets, and the Greek Θωμαΐς fold with `thomais-of-lesbos` is untouched by it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 апреля ст. ст. — «Мц. Фомаиды Египетской (476).»
source.note: The day's fourth entry and it carries no typikon icon, so no `rank` is recorded. **It keeps her on the same Julian 13 April as the Ohrid Prologue and not the 14 April of the other two calendars**, and its year, 476, is the one the Prologue already gave this folder, so nothing was widened: two sources now print it flat. The line calls her «Египетской», of Egypt, where the name page behind it (2739) heads her «Фомаида Александрийская (Египетская), мц.», of Alexandria and of Egypt both — the city that tells her from `thomais-of-lesbos`. That page gives «День памяти: 13 апреля» and no other day. The day page prints one troparion under «Молитвы», a proper of the two sisters of Bethany which belongs to the moveable Sunday the page is headed for, so no hymn was taken and this folder still has none from any source.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 14 aprilie — «Sfânta Muceniță Tomaida»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Απριλίου — «Αγία Θωμαΐς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps her, and it gives her no years. Its account agrees with the Romanian one in substance and differs in two details: it makes her husband absent on business rather than out fishing, and it names Daniel, the head of the sketis of Alexandria, as the monk who came down and took up her body. It adds the quotation it takes from Nicodemus the Hagiorite, «ἔλαβε στέφανον μάρτυρος διὰ τὴν σωφροσύνην», and the monk delivered from the passion of fornication by the oil of the lamp at her grave. Under «Ιερά Λείψανα» it puts part of her skull at the monastery of Dionysiou on Athos. The page prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.04.2026 (13. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Томаида.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, and **the Alexandrian Thomais and not the Lesbian one**: the entry's first words are „Рођена у Александрији“, and `thomais-of-lesbos` is another woman the corpus keeps on another day. **The Prologue keeps her a day earlier than either other calendar**: doxologia and saint.gr both have her on 14 April and this is the Julian 13 April. One row per church, so nothing was moved. **A death of 476 was added where this folder had none** — „Пострада св. Томаида 476. год.“, printed flat — and it is the only year any source read for this folder gives her. `node .tmp/dd.mjs 476` reads in Russian and Greek. The entry is almost all new: that she was taught piety from childhood by honourable parents and **married at fifteen**; that her father-in-law was an unclean old man who in his son's absence attacked her and meant to dishonour her; that **she warned him of the law of God even in her fear** and kept slipping out of his hands, and that after a long struggle he took a knife and killed her and **cut her in two halves**; that **God's punishment reached him in that hour — he went blind at once and could not find the door to get out**, and was caught there in the room and handed over to the court, which condemned him to death; that **many afterwards who were tormented by the passion of fornication raised prayers to her and had strong help from her**; and that **the great ascetic Daniel carried her relics to the Skete and laid them in the burial ground of the hieromonks**. **Daniel is named as the entry names him and identified with nobody**: it gives him no see, no epithet and no monastery of his own, and the corpus holds many folders of the name. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and this folder has no hymn from any source. The stored form Томаида folds with nothing.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 13 April closes its entry „Пострада св. Томаида 476. год.“ — Saint Thomais suffered in the year 476. The year is printed flat and not as «about». It is the only year any source read for this folder gives: neither doxologia.ro's notice nor saint.gr's prints one. `node .tmp/dd.mjs 476` reads in Russian and Greek.
